description: Stage 4y dedicated cases (SAFE ROLLBACK: EnableSwitchCaseClause ships DEFAULT OFF; this group is the XML/AST/fallback gate on the default raw path; the on-state readings are printed by s4y-case-clause-takeover.mjs and recorded in HANDOFF-s4y.md): clause-level statements in a switch (`case 1: f();` - no braces). The switch case-block brace gets a catalog holding ONLY CaseClauseStatementPossibleShape (never the block-body catalog: expression/variable candidates would swallow `case <expr>:` and throw SourceRange is not set, the Stage 4p failure). The candidate accepts only at the first code unit after a clause colon (or after a previous clause statement) and builds a ShellStatementFamily shell (ScanRoot end); StatementBuilder.BuildCaseBlock collects the built statement shapes into the CaseClauseShape. Each case asserts: (1) shell-path XML == legacy-path XML byte for byte; (2) AST node-for-node == ts.createSourceFile; (3) two parses give identical XML; (4) no shape/CatalogGuide leak in XML; (5) no file-level fallback. Takeover counters (SwitchCaseClauseMountCount / SwitchCaseClauseShellCount / BlockBodyStatementCount) are asserted by tests/statement-possible/s4y-case-clause-takeover.mjs and recorded in HANDOFF-s4y.md. The trap group is the safety gate: case bodies with braces, ternary case expressions, object literals, labels, nested switch, empty switch.

stage4y.stage: Stage 4y (switch clause-level statements taken over; block-level class shell behind a default-off flag)
stage4y.description: Clause-level statements (call, two statements in one clause, two clauses, default, arithmetic case expression, ternary case expression, if with a body, empty statement, let, no trailing semicolon, block-only clause, mixed clause forms, nested switch, empty switch) plus the trap group (object literal with a colon, label statement, object method containing a switch, plain switch case body).

cases.name: s4y-clause-ternary-case
cases.source: switch (x) { case a ? b : c: f(); }

cases.name: s4y-trap-switch-in-method
cases.source: const o = { m(){ switch (x) { case 1: f(); } } };

stage4aa.stage: Stage 4aa (clause shell closes at ; / EOF / ASI: StatementKind = ShellPlainExpression)
stage4aa.description: Clause-level statement takeover now delivered: multiple statements in one clause, declarations followed by statements, two clauses, ASI between clause statements (line break, and line break before the next case), case body after a clause, case body before a clause, three clauses, nested switch with two statements in the inner clause, empty statements in two clauses, default with two statements, and a switch inside a block.

cases.name: s4aa-clause-nested-switch
cases.source: switch (x) { case 1: switch (y) { case 2: f(); g(); } }

stage4ae.stage: Stage 4ae (clause statement family split: body-bearing keywords close at `}`)
stage4ae.description: A clause statement whose first code unit is a body-bearing keyword (if / for / while / do / try / with / class / function) uses the control-flow family marker: the clause shell closes at its body `}` (StatementScanner.ScanRoot) and its body brace mounts the block-body catalog, so a following clause statement is a separate shell instead of being swallowed. Covers the Stage 4ac gap ① form `case 1: if (x) { y; } b;` plus if/else, for, while, do, try, a trailing if, class and function. Every case asserts XML == legacy, AST == TS, deterministic XML, no shape leak and no file-level fallback.

cases.name: s4ae-clause-if-else
cases.source: switch (x) { case 1: if (a) { b; } else { c; } d; }

cases.name: s4ae-clause-do-body
cases.source: switch (x) { case 1: do { a; } while (b); c; }

cases.name: s4ae-clause-try-body
cases.source: switch (x) { case 1: try { a; } catch (e) { b; } c; }

cases.name: s4ae-clause-function-body
cases.source: switch (x) { case 1: function f() { g(); } b; }

stage4agsw.stage: gap-SW (switch empty clause / nested switch inner clauses / block-level class followed by a statement / function declaration body inside a clause)
stage4agsw.description: Four shapes closed together. (1) Empty clause statement: the clause shell is created AT the `;`, so `;` never becomes the shell's last code unit and the expression-family boundary (`;` / EOF / ASI) cannot conclude - `case 1: ; case 2: ;` swallowed the next clause and the whole file went through the file-level fallback. StatementEndPossibleShape.EmptyStatementEndCode now answers the one fact ScanRoot already knew (first code unit `;` => complete at that index) for every family. (2) Nested switch: a clause statement whose head is `switch` joins the body-bearing family, so the outer clause shell is a ShellStatementFamily shell, IsSwitchKeywordShell holds for it, and the INNER case block brace gets the clause catalog: inner clauses are shells too (SwitchCaseClauseShellCount / SwitchCaseClauseMountCount both 2). (3) Block-level `class C {}` followed by `f();`: ScanRoot never answered for a declaration head, so the class shell grew to the block `}` and BuildFromShell read two statements -> DetachShell -> `f();` was never replayed into the block-body catalog. StatementEndPossibleShape.DeclarationBodyEndCode closes the class shell at its body brace (StatementScanner.ScanDeclarationBody, the same judgement ScanBody already uses) and the leftover replay takes `f();` (BlockBodyStatementCount 0 -> 2). (4) `case 1: function f() { g(); }`: the function body brace's host is the clause shell, which the bracket-child hook cannot see; BlockPossibleShape.OnShellBracketCreated now mounts the block catalog on it with the same IsFunctionDeclarationBody predicate (BlockFunctionBodyMountCount 0 -> 1, BlockBodyStatementCount 0 -> 1). Every case asserts XML == legacy, AST == TS, deterministic XML, no shape leak and no file-level fallback.

cases.name: s4agsw-nested-switch-two-inner
cases.source: switch (x) { case 1: switch (y) { case 2: a; case 3: b; } }

cases.name: s4agsw-nested-switch-then-stmt
cases.source: switch (x) { case 1: switch (y) { case 2: f(); } g(); }

cases.name: s4agsw-fn-in-clause-then-stmt
cases.source: switch (x) { case 1: function f() { g(); } b; }
